hypothesis: The authority-none V58 continuous consolidator can preserve fail-closed generator identity while remaining operationally recoverable through a reviewed report-only restart whenever a loaded generator changes.
decision: Retain the fail-closed generator checksum contract and the recovered V2 recurring consolidator. Treat any generator edit as requiring a reviewed report-only process restart with a bounded cycle, focused tests, free singleton lock, two recurring publications, and unchanged live backend and venue protection. Do not automatically load changed research code into an existing process.
falsifier: Revise this disposition if the recurring V2 consolidator stops while all required sources and generator hashes remain unchanged, fails to publish twice after the reviewed restart, changes live backend or venue state, accepts a changed generator without terminating, or publishes any authority/live-change contract other than none/false.
limitations: Two recurring publications do not prove indefinite availability; output freshness and process state remain required telemetry.
The report-only process has no external supervisor that can distinguish a reviewed generator deployment from an accidental edit.
Automatic restart after a generator change would silently load new research code and is intentionally not enabled.
The recovery validates technical observability, not strategy profitability or an exit recommendation.
ETH and SP500 remain open, so their marked economics are provisional and terminal reconciliation is still required.
